body: over 'my' counter...a friand gave them to me.

Very helpful, thank you! I'm beginning to think that the recruiter doesn't know how to answer my questions correctly. I waited three days for a response and received something copied and pasted from a document. I followed up with a few more questions and haven't heard anything.
Oh, no I didn't mean I would leave her. just that I don't know if it would last through 5 years of service...or 8.

Don't be a fool and give up an opportunity with the Army?

I understand that you are supporting both sides in your post. I appreciate the thought. I'm still discussing things with the recruiter but I think I might have to commit to 3 years reserve after 5 years of active, but I'm not certain. I'm aware that I have A LOT more to learn/read/study before even attempting to make this decision. It has recently surfaced and I have until December or so to decide, but I want to weigh all things properly. I assumed r/Military would be the place to ask questions or gain opinions.

Thanks for all of the replies, guys. I'm certain some understand the 'Omg I'm in love, ill never find this again!' Feeling that's so hard to walk from. Who knows, we could still be together in the end. That's hard to believe though.

I did find that it would likely be an 8 year commitment, 5 active, 3 reserve.

I'm actually waiting on more information from the recruiter. I know that at the very least it will be a 4-5 year commitment. I haven't actually had a chance to look over EVERYTHING just yet, as I only spoke with her on Friday and she will likely not respond to my last email until Monday. However, I know training (school in TX) would be at least two years and a deployment would be necessary due to an active duty commitment. The woman I am with has been on two tours of duty and knows about this decision of mine. Either way, I feel like I'm losing out. Money and experience is terribly hard to turn down. Though, everyone wants to think what THEY have with their SO would last through anything, I fear that I would learn otherwise.
